examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Classify ACID by the observed failure: atomicity is all-or-nothing, consistency preserves invariants, isolation prevents harmful concurrent interference, durability retains committed results after crashes. A lost update can violate isolation and a conservation invariant without proving that a crash-related durability failure occurred.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A committed transaction's modified data page has not reached disk, but redo logging restores it after a crash. How many of the four ACID properties does this scenario directly demonstrate?

**Answer: 1.** It directly demonstrates durability: committed effects survive the crash via redo recovery. The scenario alone does not establish all-or-nothing execution, invariant preservation or isolation for other transactions, so the directly evidenced count is one.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An application can violate an invariant even when a storage engine supplies atomic commits; transactional consistency also depends on correct application logic.

Consistency is about defined invariants, not a claim that every application transaction is automatically correct.
